events.title: Google Public Sector Summit
events.location: Ronald Reagan Building and International Trade Center, 1300 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.description: Industry summit flagged by ETI for its tech and defense sessions: AI-era mission data, agentic AI across government (CDAO, NOAA, NVIDIA speakers), predictive Army sustainment, and securing the agentic era with Navy and NNSA.
events.why: Shows how DoD and civilian agencies are actually buying and deploying agentic AI, a short walk from SAIS.

events.title: Boundary Breakers Student Pre-Mixer
events.location: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.host: VentureNEST, SAIS Entrepreneurship Club and SAIS Tech Club
events.description: Student mixer for Baltimore and DC campuses ahead of the Boundary Breakers national-security tech showcase (DC Startup & Tech Week). Free for students; light refreshments.
events.why: Networking warm-up with JHU founders and engineers before the ETI-co-hosted defense-tech showcase.

events.title: Africa's Innovation Economy: Careers, Technology, and Opportunity
events.location: Room B244, Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.host: SAIS BSU, Africa Club, Technology Club, Africa and T&I Focus Areas, Global Careers
events.description: Conversation with Caleb Maru, founder and CEO of Tech Safari and The Big Move, on Africa's innovation ecosystem, emerging tech trends, entrepreneurship, diaspora engagement and careers. SAIS/Hopkins students only.
events.why: T&I-co-sponsored look at African tech ecosystems and career paths for students working at the tech-development intersection.

events.title: Disrupting Politics: A Conversation with Katie Harbath
events.location: Room 422, Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.description: Fireside chat with Anchor Change founder and former Facebook executive Katie Harbath on her book Disrupting Politics: platforms and elections, the 2016 election, dismantled integrity teams and governing online speech. Moderated by Olga Belogolova; lunch served.
events.why: ETI flagship event on platform integrity and election policy with a former Facebook policy leader, in Room 422.

events.title: AI-Enabled Energy Systems Conference: Technologies, Intelligence, and Security
events.host: JHU Data Science and AI Institute, ROSEI and HEMI
events.description: Researchers from academia, industry and government on AI across the energy ecosystem, from materials design and grid infrastructure to system operations, reliability and security.
events.why: Relevant to AI-energy policy but technical and held in Baltimore, so a stretch for DC students.

events.title: Astropolitics in the Americas: Latin America's Place in the New Space Race
events.location: Room 258, Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.host: SAIS Americas Focus Area / Latin America Studies Initiative
events.description: Americas Lunch Speaker Series #4 with space policy and international cooperation expert Laura Delgado López (AzurX, FIU) on Latin America's bid to play a bigger role in the space economy. Lunch provided.
events.why: Rare on-campus space-policy talk that looks at the space economy from outside the US-China frame.

events.title: U.S. Shipbuilding Cooperation: Collaboration with South Korea and other Allies
events.location: Room 1024, Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.description: Discussion of US shipbuilding revival and industrial cooperation with South Korea and other allies. Listed in the SAIS Upcoming Events digest; open to the SAIS community.
events.why: Allied defense-industrial policy rather than technology per se; peripheral to ETI.

events.title: Past, Present, Prompted: DPRK Hacking Enters the AI Era
events.location: Room 222, Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.host: SAIS Asia Focus Area (Asia Policy & Career Roundtable Series)
events.description: Cyber threat intelligence analyst Daniel Gordon, a specialist on North Korean hacking with a decade in CTI and incident response, on how DPRK cyber operations are adapting to AI. Lunch for registered guests; cross-posted to sais.ti.
events.why: Practitioner briefing on AI-enabled state hacking, squarely in the cyber-and-AI lane ETI covers.

events.title: Counterintelligence, Insider Risk, and the Emerging Threat Landscape
events.location: Room 258, Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.host: SAIS Defense and Intelligence Club and US Focus Area
events.description: Panel of national security professionals with USG and private-sector experience on counterintelligence, insider risk and the emerging threat landscape. Lunch at 12:15.
events.why: Security-adjacent career panel; technology is not the stated focus.

events.title: Johns Hopkins Sesquicentennial Symposium on The Future of Technology Transfer and Academic Innovation
events.location: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.description: One-day symposium on technology transfer and academic entrepreneurship policy, with NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya, NSF Director James O'Neill and panels on dual-use technology, federal translation programs and corporate partnerships.
events.why: Federal R&D and dual-use tech-transfer policy with the NIH and NSF directors, in the SAIS building.

events.title: Envisioning the Future of National Security: Healthcare Resilience and Predictive Innovation in an Era of Hybrid Warfare
events.location: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.host: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health and Uniformed Services University
events.description: Conference on how military conflict shapes biomedical innovation, pharmaceutical supply-chain vulnerabilities, and how AI can predict disruptions and strengthen readiness. Keynote by Keith Bass, Assistant Secretary of War for Health Affairs.
events.why: Biotech supply-chain security and AI for readiness, promoted by ETI and held in the SAIS building.

events.title: Code, Country, and Contracts: Demystifying China's Cyber Ecosystem
events.location: Room 422, Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.host: SAIS Technology & Innovation and China Focus Areas (T&I Speaker Series)
events.description: Panel on China's cyber ecosystem from 1990s patriotic hackers to state-linked contractors like i-SOON, the post-Snowden talent pipeline, and how researchers unmask Chinese hacking groups. Moderated by Prof. Melissa Griffith; lunch from 12:45.
events.why: T&I flagship panel with leading China-cyber researchers, in Room 422.

events.title: Reflections on Promoting Innovation in Defense: Madeline Hart (Palantir)
events.location: Room 422, Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.host: Philip Merrill Center for Strategic Studies (Defense Industry Speaker Series)
events.description: Conversation and Q&A led by Prof. Thomas Mahnken with Palantir national security lead Madeline Hart, author of Mobilize, on the changing defense industrial ecosystem and careers in defense tech. Lunch provided.
events.why: Defense-tech industrial-base debate and careers from a Palantir insider, cross-posted to sais.ti.

events.title: The Future of Next: Johns Hopkins 150th Anniversary Capstone
events.location: Johns Hopkins University Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.description: Anniversary-closing day of talks on the future of health, technology, democracy, cities and the arts. Keynote by Kevin Ashton, who coined the term Internet of Things; panelists include Atul Gawande and Anne Applebaum. Free, limited seating.
events.why: Broad university showcase in the SAIS building with only some technology content.

events.title: The Bitter Struggle: Superintelligence, Superpowers, and the Fate of the World
events.location: Room 822, Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.description: Prof. Ben Buchanan, former White House Special Advisor for AI, and NYT correspondent David Sanger discuss Buchanan's new book: US-China AI competition, whether export controls just buy time, frontier-lab power and democratic values. Books for sale; refreshments.
events.why: Book launch by SAIS's own former White House AI adviser on AI and great-power competition.

events.title: Off-Grid Building Tour
events.location: Arlington, VA (three blocks from Clarendon Metro)
events.host: SAIS Development, Climate, and Sustainability Focus Area
events.description: Prof. Johannes Urpelainen leads a tour of Prof. Scott Sklar's two fully off-grid buildings: solar PV, wind, battery banks, geothermal cooling, solar water heating and a hydrogen fuel cell. Current SAIS students; capped at 20.
events.why: Hands-on look at distributed clean-energy tech; more climate than tech policy.

events.title: Africa and the AI Economy
events.location: Rooms 940/944, Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.host: SAIS Tech Club, SAIS Africa Club, Village Ties and Africa Business Club
events.description: Panel on how Africa can seize AI-driven opportunities in technology, digital infrastructure and investment, with Kenya's Deputy Chief of Mission and leaders from Amazon, Cassava Technologies and Fonbnk. Moderated by Hanan Awel; networking and light bites.
events.why: Tech Club panel on AI infrastructure and Africa's place in the global AI economy, promoted by T&I.

events.title: CYBERWARCON 2026
events.location: Hyatt Regency Crystal City, Arlington, VA
events.description: Annual cyber conflict conference. ETI circulated a call for student volunteers (free registration; background check and Nov 3 virtual orientation required); the volunteer deadline was Oct 23.
events.why: Premier DC-area cyber threat-intel conference with strong SAIS/Alperovitch ties; volunteering earns free entry.

events.title: Lessons in Leadership: Navigating Digital Democracy
events.location: Kenney Link (Rooms 426/428/430), Hopkins Bloomberg Center, 555 Pennsylvania Ave NW
events.host: Latin America Studies Initiative, SAIS Women Lead and Global Women in Leadership
events.description: Day of conversations with women leaders from Latin America and Africa on defending democracy in the digital age: election monitoring, countering disinformation and online harassment, and technology as both tool and threat. Lunch served.
events.why: Disinformation and online-harassment policy content, in the SAIS building.
